findings.title: Docs say the Operator fails without `rolling-updates`, but no Operator check is added
findings.body:
The new CAUTION block says that during preview the `rolling-updates` feature must be enabled, "Otherwise, the Keycloak Operator will fail." This PR adds no Operator code that reads `spec.features` or gates `spec.update.strategy` on that feature. The only Operator-side changes are the test CR and the test Dockerfile.

As a result, a CR with `update.strategy: Recreate` and no `rolling-updates` feature behaves exactly as before, and nothing fails. Either the enforcement is missing (for example, a status error when an update strategy is set without the feature) or the documentation is wrong.

The `UpgradeTest` change only enables the feature on the happy path. No test checks that the Operator rejects or flags a strategy when the feature is disabled, so the documented behavior is not verified.

findings.title: Appended `--features=rolling-updates` overrides the user's own features configuration
findings.body:
The `updatecompatibility` macro now always appends `--features=rolling-updates` after the user's parameters. The guide tells users to run `metadata`/`check` with exactly the same configuration options as their deployment, including env vars and CLI args.

If a deployment sets features via `KC_FEATURES`, `keycloak.conf`, or its own `--features=...`, this appended CLI option either takes precedence and replaces that list, or duplicates the option. In both cases the metadata is generated for a feature set that differs from the deployment's. Once metadata includes configuration, this can produce a wrong rolling/recreate verdict.

The guide should tell users to add `rolling-updates` to their existing feature list (or use `--profile=preview`) instead of appending a separate `--features` option.

findings.title: New feature changes `--features` help output; approval files not updated
findings.body:
Adding `ROLLING_UPDATES` adds `rolling-updates` to the possible values of the `--features` / `--features-disabled` options, which are generated from `Profile.Feature`. That list is printed in the CLI help, and the help approval files in the quarkus integration tests capture it for `start`, `start-dev`, `build`, `export`, `import`, `update-compatibility`, etc.

None of those approved files are updated in this PR. The help approval tests are expected to fail until they are regenerated.

findings.title: New exit codes (3 = recreate, 4 = feature disabled) are not asserted
findings.body:
The PR renumbers `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from 4 to 3 and gives 4 to the new `FEATURE_DISABLED` result. The docs present these exit codes as the scripting contract.

However:
- `testFeatureNotEnabled` only checks the error message, and only for the `metadata` subcommand. The `check` subcommand's feature gate is untested, and exit code 4 is never asserted.
- `testWrongVersions` only checks the error text, not that the exit code is now 3.

A regression in either mapping, such as recreate and feature-disabled colliding again, would go unnoticed.
